name: per-tensor-quantized-sdpa-tile-zero-selector
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: Function constant 123 zeroes the input-type selectors. No per-tensor SDPA specialization accepts the resulting state, so the entry returns before resource or threadgroup-memory access; the one-lane exact observation remains unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: per-tensor-tile-8x8x8-int8-kv-six-rows-28-keys-edges
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-selector case of this entry, whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. Constant 123 selects the float-query, int8-key/value path (input types 11, 1, 11: the 8x8 simdgroup-matrix instantiation) and constant 115 its multi-simdgroup-per-row form with a matrix mask, the AGX3 emask path, threadgroup tile 8 rows x 16 keys, simdgroup tiles 8x8, K tile 8 and threadgroup O reduction off, so the result is stored directly into oArray (binding 28) and the first context tile's normalized result goes through the O-sum workspace (binding 27). Constant 122 binds a seven-entry table: Q entry 0, int8 K entry 2 and V entry 3, mask entry 4, and the per-tensor K scale 0.25 (entry 5) and V scale 0.5 (entry 6). One threadgroup of two simdgroups; alpha 2, so every score is the int8 dot product times kScale x alpha = 0.5. queryLength 6 of the 8 tile rows, contextLength 28 = one full and one partial 16-key context tile, dimsPerHead 12 with paddedDimsPerHead 16, so the edge checks drop rows 6-7, keys 28-31 and dims 12-15 (K and V rows are packed at 12 bytes, so an unchecked dim read would take the next key); oArray holds 6 rows of stride 16 whose dims 12-15 keep the 0xab fill. Key n belongs to one of four groups; query row r holds 400 at its group's one-hot dimension plus small terms shared per group, so every key of the row's group scores the row maximum and every other key at least 176 below (exp underflows to 0 everywhere); the mask adds a row shift and removes (-1000) the row's group keys it does not keep. The kept keys per row and context tile keep every running sum a power of two (a row with no kept key in the first tile is rescaled by exp of at most -176 = 0), every softmax weight is 0 or exp(0) = 1, and each output is the V scale 0.5 times the mean of 1, 2, 4 or 8 small int8 values of V, exact. Every loop is finite by these inputs: two context tiles, two 8-deep K steps, one 16-wide output-dim chunk.

name: sampled-background-uniform-texture
rationale: The loop-free fragment samples a one-pixel RGBA32Float texture at the generated float2 varying and multiplies it by an authored 0.5 fade; the uniform texel makes the sample independent of interpolation and address mode while the RGBA16Float attachment records the exact converted result.

name: radix-256-histogram-of-a-shifted-byte-with-a-partial-tail
rationale:
The device evidence for `passes/workgroup/atomic_loop.rs`, the coverage queue's head at 14 of 28 reached functions with no authored case. `apply_unroll_plan`, `remap_operand`, `splice_unrolled_preheader` and `unique_unconditional_preheader` -- the whole unroll funnel -- had never executed under any case. An eprintln on each, swept over all 14,579 sources, found 42 modules that reach them and not one of them cased; this is the smallest, at 166 lines. Measured with covgain against every cased corpus source plus every public fixture: 10 functions no cased source reaches, 9 in `atomic_loop.rs` and one in `passes/access/workgroup.rs`.

The shape the rule is named for: a threadgroup-atomic accumulation inside a literal-bounded loop, which the pass unrolls. Each of the 256 threads holds two keys in a private `[2 x int]`, reads byte `pass` out of each, and does an `air.atomic.local.add.u.i32` into a 256-entry threadgroup histogram; the addend is the bounds predicate `index < num_keys` rather than a constant, so the atomic is what carries the guard. Two barriers bracket it, and the same 256 threads zero the histogram before and drain it after.

`pass` is 2, so the bucket is byte 2 of the key, and every key's low half is the literal 0xCDAB. A lost or wrong shift therefore does not perturb the histogram, it collapses it: shift 0 piles all 500 counts onto bucket 171 and shift 8 onto bucket 205, against 244 twos and 12 ones spread over every bucket. `num_keys` is 500 of the 512 keys the 256 threads read, so buckets 0..243 are hit twice and 244..255 once -- the split is exactly where the second key of a thread falls past the end, so dropping the bounds predicate makes all 256 buckets read 2 and nothing else changes. Losing an unrolled iteration halves every count instead.

The output buffer is 2,048 bytes and compared whole while the kernel writes only its first 1,024, over a 0xAB fill, so a drain that walks past the histogram is visible. The two loops each run exactly twice on a literal induction variable that no input can change, hence `authored_bounded`.

name: argmax-unsigned-uint8-with-a-padded-index-value-pair
rationale:
No authored case reached `llvm.memset.p3.i64`, which 6 corpus sources name. All six are the same MLX kernel, `arg_reduce_general<uchar|bool, ArgMax, 4>`, and this 354-line `argmax_uint8` is the smallest. Its argument metadata is byte-identical to the already-cased `argmax_int8`, so the same eight buffers and the same shape parameters serve both, and the input bytes are deliberately the SAME ones -- which is what lets the two cases be read against each other.

Say plainly what the memset does here, because it decides what the case can claim. The threadgroup array is `[32 x IndexValPair]`, and `IndexValPair` is a `uint` index at byte 0, a `uchar` value at byte 4, and three bytes of padding at 5, 6 and 7. The call zeroes exactly those three padding bytes, and nothing in the kernel ever reads them: the cross-lane reduction that follows loads the index at offset 0 and the value at offset 4. So the memset's EFFECT is unobservable, and this case does not pretend to observe it. What it observes is that the write lands where AIR says and disturbs neither field beside it. A lowering that lost the `+5` byte offset and zeroed from the start of the pair would clear the low three bytes of every thread's index after it was stored; each thread only touches its own pair, so that is deterministic, and both rows would then answer index 0 instead of 1 and 5.

The second thing the case separates is the unsigned comparison, which is why the input is the cased signed case's input unchanged. Row 0 is 3, 255, 2, 254, 7, 253, 5, 247, 248, 250 and row 1 is 7, 156, 120, 127, 0, 255, 127, 5, 253, 12. Read as `uchar` the maxima are 255 at index 1 and 255 at index 5; read as `char` -- which is what the sibling `argmax_int8` case pins -- the same twenty bytes answer 4 and 3. So the two cases share an input and must disagree, and a host lowered with the wrong signedness produces the OTHER case's expected output rather than something obviously broken.

The dispatch is two threadgroups of thirty-two threads with `ndim` 1, `shape` (2), `in_strides` (10), `out_strides` (1), `axis_stride` 1 and `axis_size` 10, so threads 0..31 reduce row 0 and 32..63 reduce row 1. Each thread takes four consecutive axis elements, so row 0's winner sits in thread 0's window and row 1's in thread 1's -- the pair reduction across threads has to run for either row to come out right, which is what makes a clobbered pair visible at all. The input buffer carries four bytes past the two rows that the `axis_size` guard must never read, and the output buffer is four words of which only two are written; the other two must keep their 0x9C poison. `execution_safety` is `authored_bounded` for the same six CFG cycles the sibling case enumerates.

name: single-mip-quad-viewer-passes-each-texel-through-unscaled
rationale: The shader lays a texture's mip chain out as nested rectangles and shows whichever level covers the fragment. air.get_num_mip_levels_texture_2d picks the layout: 0 discards, 1 gives the full unit rectangle, anything larger gives a 2/3-wide one. With a single-level texture the count is 1, so the rectangle is (0,0,1,1), the divide by its width is the identity and level 0 is sampled at the fragment's own uv. That makes the query observable rather than decorative -- a lowering that reported 0 would discard every fragment, and one that reported 2 would rescale u by 3/2 and push the right-hand column outside the rectangle. On a 2x2 target the uv values are 0.25 and 0.75, exactly the texel centres of a 2x2 source, so the sampler's linear filter returns the texel itself and the case does not depend on the filter. Every source channel is exactly representable in half, so the f32-to-f16 narrowing on the way out is exact, and no alpha is -1, which is the sentinel the shader uses to mean 'not covered'.

name: rope-flushed-lane-beside-an-evaluated-one
rationale: Two threads take the two arms of Metal's fast::sin / fast::cos flush in one dispatch. The rotation angle is scale * fast_exp2(-base * pos.x / grid.x) * offset. Lane 0 has pos.x = 0, so the exponent is -0.0, exp2 is 1.0 and the angle is exactly 1.0e7 -- past float(pi/2) * 2^22, the largest magnitude the hardware still evaluates -- so both fast::cos and fast::sin answer exactly 0.0 and both of lane 0's outputs are 0.0 whatever the inputs were. Lane 1 has pos.x = 1 and base 400, so the exponent is exactly -200 and exp2 underflows, leaving an angle of zero (or below 2^-149): cos is 1.0 and sin is 0.0 or absorbed, so lane 1 copies its two inputs through unchanged. Reading [0, 3, 0, 7] therefore pins both arms of the flush select, and every value is an exact float.

name: sparse-sample-of-an-argument-buffer-texture-returns-its-value-where-resident
rationale: The fragment function's constant argument buffer 0 is SparseMaterial {texture2d<half> t; uint min_mip;}, t a 2x2 rgba16_float texture of one level that is not sparse, holding texel (x, y) = (1 + x + 2y, (x + 1) / 2, (y + 1) / 4, 1), and min_mip 0. It samples t with sparse_sample through a constexpr sampler with linear min, mag and mip filters, repeat addressing and max_anisotropy 10. The generated passthrough vertex draws the fullscreen triangle with uv = (ndc + 1) / 2, so each pixel center has uv 0.25 or 0.75 on each axis, the center of one texel, and uv moves by one texel per pixel: level 0, the texel itself under every filter. Metal's target origin is the top left with NDC y up, so target pixel (px, py) reads texel (px, 1 - py). Metal reports a texture that is not sparse resident everywhere. The function returns the sparse sample's value where resident() holds, else the sample clamped by min_lod_clamp(min_mip); the front end merges the two {half4, i8} results in a phi. Row 0 holds (3, 0.5, 0.5, 1), (4, 1, 0.5, 1) and row 1 (1, 0.5, 0.25, 1), (2, 1, 0.25, 1), every value exact in binary16 and distinct per pixel.

name: sparse-sample-of-an-argument-buffer-texture-states-it-resident
rationale: The fragment function's constant argument buffer 0 is SparseMaterial {texture2d<half> t; uint min_mip;}, t a 2x2 rgba16_float texture of one level that is not sparse, holding texel (x, y) = (1 + x + 2y, (x + 1) / 2, (y + 1) / 4, 1), and min_mip 0. It samples t with sparse_sample through a constexpr sampler with linear min, mag and mip filters, repeat addressing and max_anisotropy 10. The generated passthrough vertex draws the fullscreen triangle with uv = (ndc + 1) / 2, so each pixel center has uv 0.25 or 0.75 on each axis, the center of one texel, and uv moves by one texel per pixel: level 0, the texel itself under every filter. Metal's target origin is the top left with NDC y up, so target pixel (px, py) reads texel (px, 1 - py). Metal reports a texture that is not sparse resident everywhere. The function returns the sparse sample's first two channels, then 0.25 where resident() holds and 0.75 where it does not, then 1. Row 0 holds (3, 0.5, 0.25, 1), (4, 1, 0.25, 1) and row 1 (1, 0.5, 0.25, 1), (2, 1, 0.25, 1): every pixel resident.

name: identity-rotation-turns-a-zero-log-scale-into-a-diagonal-covariance
rationale: Straight-line apart from a three-way switch on the activation type, so execution_safety is loop_free. activation_scale is 1, which is the arm that calls air.fast_exp.v3f32, and the stage-in scale is exactly zero, so the transcendental's result is exactly (1, 1, 1) and nothing rests on how either runtime rounds an exponential. That matters twice over: a fast_exp that returned anything but 1 would scale the whole covariance, and dropping the call entirely would take the switch's identity arm and hand on (0, 0, 0), which zeroes all six outputs. The rotation is the identity quaternion (1, 0, 0, 0), whose dot with itself is 1, so air.fast_rsqrt.f32 is exactly 1 as well and the normalized quaternion is unchanged; every off-diagonal of the rotation matrix is then a product of zeros. With scale_modifier 2 the scale matrix is diag(2, 2, 2) and the written upper triangle of M*Mt is (4, 0, 0, 4, 0, 4). The three exact zeros are the load-bearing part: they say the rotation collapsed to the identity and the off-diagonal terms cancelled, and the 0xAB fill makes a store the translator drops read back as 0xABABABAB rather than as a plausible float.

name: planar-edge-alpha

name: reads-through-an-index-past-an-argument-buffers-texture-array
rationale: Eight threads (the handle array index form). The argument buffer ts (binding 1) holds the two-texture array tex at bytes 0 and 8 and, after it, the two-texture array spare at bytes 16 and 24: 1x1 r32_uint textures holding 0xE1000000, 0xE1000001, 0xE2000000, 0xE2000001. idx = 0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3. Thread t reads texel (0, 0) of tex[idx[t]] into out[t] (threads 4 to 7 index past tex into the handles the argument buffer holds after it, a result Metal leaves undefined: out bytes 16 to 31 are the declared out-of-bounds reads), and texel (0, 0) of spare[t & 1] into out[8 + t]. The output is out: tex's texels twice, the four reads, then spare's texels four times.

name: depth-multisampled-array-reads-at-32-and-16-bit-coordinates

Texture 0 a depth 2D multisampled array depth32_float 3 x 2, 3 slices, 4 samples, read texture, every sample a distinct float in (0, 1) over many binades, written per sample. Lane i reads sample i mod 4 of texel ((i / 4) mod 3, (i / 12) mod 2) in slice (i / 24) mod 3 at 32- and 16-bit coordinates and writes the two depths' words to out[i] of buffer 0 (uint2 elements), pre-filled with 0xAB. 128 lanes, so every sample is read; every coordinate is inside. The AIR has no loop.

name: interpolate-a-control-point-texcoord-across-a-one-factor-triangle-patch
rationale:
The first authored case that executes a post-tessellation vertex function. 233 of the 14579 corpus sources are one -- the largest single family with no device evidence of any kind -- and until now the whole tessellation path had only unit tests: candidate.rs synthesizes a Vulkan tessellation-control companion because Metal has no control stage, and both that companion and Metal's factor buffer plus drawPatches had been asserted to assemble and encode, never to run.

eMHMCLaTPglgf6yx is a triangle patch of 3 control points carrying position, texcoord and normal at locations 0, 1 and 2. Its texcoord output is the barycentric blend of the three control-point texcoords with the second lane flipped to 1 - v, so the observation is a pure function of TessCoord and the control-point fetch with no buffer or texture in the path.

Edge factors 1, 1, 1 and inside factor 1 make the tessellator emit exactly one triangle whose three TessCoords are the corners (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (0,0,1). The shader maps t to cp0*t.x + cp1*t.y + cp2*t.z, so whichever order the tessellator emits those corners in, the three generated vertices carry exactly cp0, cp1 and cp2 -- the case cannot be moved by tessellator vertex ordering, but it still fails if the domain, the control-point fetch, or the correspondence between a TessCoord component and a control-point index is wrong.

The control-point positions are the standard full-coverage triangle (-1,-1), (3,-1), (-1,3) with w = 1, so all 16 pixels of the 4x4 target are covered and interpolation is affine. The texcoords (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1) make u the rasterizer weight of control point 1 and v that of control point 2, each an exact multiple of 1/16 at these pixel centres. Exchanging control points 1 and 2 leaves the triangle's coverage identical and only swaps u with 1 - v, so the bytes still move; a symmetric choice of texcoords could not see that.

Everything else is neutralized. mvp_i is the identity, so the clip position is the interpolated control point. The displacement normalize(interp_normal) * (disp_map.x - 0.5) is exactly zero: all three control-point normals are (0,0,1) so the interpolated normal is (0,0,1) and its inverse square root is exactly 1, and the 1x1 disp_map holds 0.5, so the scale is exactly 0. mvp_j feeds only varying 0, which this case does not observe.

Metal writes u = (x_ndc + 1)/4 along each row and 1 - (y_ndc + 1)/4 down each column, that is 0.0625, 0.1875, 0.3125, 0.4375 crossed with 0.5625, 0.6875, 0.8125, 0.9375, which is what the solve above predicts. MoltenVK matches exactly. No executor change was needed: the candidate already requests tessellationShader and refuses a tessellation reflection without it.

name: initialize-signed-minmax
rationale: The loop-free entry unconditionally stores INT_MAX and INT_MIN into adjacent aligned i32 elements of its sole read/write buffer, replacing the full eight-byte poisoned selection.

name: float-to-half-rounding-at-the-half-range-edge-and-denormals-under-fast-math
rationale: Thread i reads the float vectors (x, y, z) from in[3i .. 3i + 2] and writes 16 words, each 4-lane half result as two words (lane 0 in the low half of the first): half(x), half(y), hx + hy, hx * hy, hx - hy, fma(hx, hy, hz), half(x * y) and hx * hy + hz, where hx, hy and hz are half(x), half(y) and half(z). x runs over the edge of the half range of both signs (65504 and its float neighbours, 65512 and its neighbours, the largest float below 65520, 65520 and above, 65536, 1e5, infinity), ties of the half normal grid (2049, 2051, 4097, 1 + 2^-11) and the half denormals and their ties (2^-25, 3 * 2^-26, 2^-24, 2^-15, below 2^-14); y and z bring sums, differences and products of halves onto the same edges. It measures how Metal rounds a float to half there: to nearest even, every value from 65504 up to below 65520 to 65504 and from 65520 up to infinity. Compiled with the default fast math: the half arithmetic carries every flag.

name: gelu-saturates-fast-tanh-on-both-sides-of-the-clamp
rationale: Three invocations of the GELU activation, each writing one element, chosen so air.fast_tanh.f32 is byte-exact in all three: tanh saturates to exactly 1.0f in binary32 for arguments past about 9.011, so an argument well beyond that has one representable answer no matter how the function is approximated, while an unsaturated argument would differ by a ULP between the Metal oracle and the recompiled candidate. Lane 0 takes 30, whose inner polynomial reaches about 987 and is cut down by air.fast_clamp.f32 to the 30 the shader allows. Lane 1 takes 8, whose inner polynomial reaches about 24.65 and passes the clamp untouched, so the two lanes cover both sides of it. Lane 2 takes -8 and saturates the other way, making 1 + tanh exactly zero and the product a negative zero, which both backends produce. The results (30, 8, -0) are the identity on the saturated side, so a tanh that stops short of one moves every lane.

name: gpu-encoded-buffers-keep-the-host-encoded-dispatches
rationale: The host encodes each command's dispatch of 64 threads in groups of 8 (command 0 as threads, command 1 as 8 threadgroups with a barrier) and its 32-byte threadgroup length; then two producer threads each set only command t's kernel buffers 0 and 1, the params window and the out window at 256 * t bytes. The commands inherit the pipeline: the execution's parent is the template icb_replay_template (token 2, the template's own case). Executing them after the producer observes that the GPU's buffer setters keep the host's dispatch and length: window 0's params are scale 2 and bias 1, window 1's scale 9 and bias 4, so out holds 2 * t + 3 for t in 0..64, then 9 * t + 13. Every selected byte differs from the 0xab fill.

name: threadgroup-record-copy-decomposes-a-flat-leaf-index
rationale:
A whole-record assignment between two elements of a `threadgroup` array parameter, which is the only shape in the corpus that leaves a flat one-index access chain for `passes::resources::rewrites::structural_load` to decompose. Measured with per-function coverage against every cased source: this fixture reaches 5 functions no cased source reaches, being every one of that file's unverified rules -- `split_flat_workgroup_index`, `decompose_flattened_struct_index`, `scaled_record_index`, `homogeneous_leaf_count` and `coerce_workgroup_index_to_uint`. Before it, the whole family was reached by exactly one of the 14,579 corpus sources: an 841-line tiled prefix-sum kernel, uncased.

Why this shape and not the obvious one. `tile[tid].a = v` alone does NOT reach the repair: the frontend emits a two-index `getelementptr` and the translator builds a correctly typed `OpAccessChain %_ptr_Workgroup_uint %tile %record %member` directly, so the pointee already equals the leaf and the rule declines. The repair only has work to do when a chain names the RECORD and a leaf is loaded through it, and the frontend produces that from a struct assignment -- `llvm.memcpy.p3.p3.i64` between two `getelementptr %struct.Bucket, ptr addrspace(3) %tile, i64 %i` pointers that carry no member index at all. `Bucket` is four `uint` leaves so `homogeneous_leaf_count` answers 4, and the flat index the memcpy expansion produces is `i * 4 + member`, which is exactly the `IMul`-then-`IAdd` form `scaled_record_index` and `decompose_flattened_struct_index` are written to recognise.

No thread writes a location another thread writes. Thread t fills record t, then after the barrier copies record `(t + 1) & 7` into record `t + 8`, a slot only thread t touches, and reads its four leaves back. The barrier orders the fill against the neighbour read; the copy and the read-back need none, being the same thread. So the comparison is exact without depending on any interleaving.

The answer is derived, not observed-then-blessed. With `in[t] = 10t + 1`, record t holds (v, v+1, v+2, v+3) for v = in[t], and the read-back weights those leaves 1, 2, 4 and 8, so `out[t] = 15 * in[src] + 34` for `src = (t + 1) & 7`, which is `150 * src + 49`: 199, 349, 499, 649, 799, 949, 1099, 49. The weights are distinct powers of two, so a swapped or dropped member is visible rather than silent, and the rotation by one makes a decomposition that loses the record index answer another thread's record. The output buffer starts at 0xffffffff in every word, which no arm can produce.

`loop_free`: the entry has no loop and no call. The dispatch is one threadgroup of eight threads, the literal length of the input the kernel indexes; the threadgroup allocation is 16 records of 16 bytes, twice the eight the kernel fills, because the copy destination is `tid + 8`.

name: linked-gather-vector-matrix-bfloat-k439-second-matrix-tg-reduction
rationale: Reaching variant of e7c7d76a (linked-zero-k-gather-vector-matrix-bfloat), whose zero kernel-info word and params leave the kernel no K and no rows. The constants select an Apple device (constant 127 bit 10) whose threadgroup shape comes from the kernel-info word: 8 simdgroups, 32 threads along K and 8 rows (grid and threadgroup 32x8x1); the gather (constant 124 bit 13, every threadgroup id kept), 4-wide B loads, a K tile of 2, the partial reduction step, the K tail (not divisible by 4), the alpha multiply, the y edge check, the threadgroup-memory reduction (no simd reduction: 1024 bytes, one float per thread) and the linked destination callback. N = 8 rows of K = 439: the two whole steps (numDeviceReductionsDownTileK 2) cover elements 0 to 255, the partial steps 2 and 3 (numDeviceReductions 4) elements 256 to 435 (K4 = 436: lanes 0 to 12 of step 3), and thread 0 of each row the tail 436 to 438. P = 1 and indices[0] = 1, so the kernel reads the second of two bfloat A matrices (AMatrixBytes = 8 rows of 440 elements): A_e[n][k] = (5k + 3n + floor(kn/4) + 2e) mod 7 - 3, so expert 0 would give other sums; B[k] = (3k + floor(k/5)) mod 5 - 1 (bfloat, BRowBytes one element). Thread (0, n) writes alpha * D[n] (alpha 0.5) through the callback at coordinate n: table entry 1's 8 floats, each written once. Every product is an integer of magnitude at most 9 and every partial sum an integer below 2^12, exact in float in any order, and the alpha product is exact. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the step counts, K4 and the constant thread counts bound the reduction loops, and the tree halves 32 to 1.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-vector-matrix-bfloat

rationale: The zero kernel-info word sets the reduction tile, SIMD count, K extent, postfix-link flag, and fusion modes to zero.
